summary: Measured on the same 25 features, ING sits clearly with the traditional banks (position score 0.13): its offer is clearer than the peer mean (5.0 vs 3.83) and it quotes far more figures (25.5 vs 12.1), but it has by far the fewest calls to action (3.0 vs 13.75), no comparison table and no mobile-first design signal. The two priorities are therefore to turn the campaign pages into a shorter, mobile-first route with repeated calls to action, and to place conditions beside every 'free' claim. None of this is performance evidence: the captured pages span three product families and two languages and come from a single capture day, so every recommendation below is a hypothesis to test.

recommendations.title: Cut the number of quoted figures per page
recommendations.finding: Figures and percentages quoted is ING's largest positive deviation: 25.5 per page against a peer mean of 12.1, a gap of 1.61 standard deviations. Clarity of the offer is also above the peer mean (5.0 vs 3.83), so the volume of numbers is not the thing carrying the clarity.
recommendations.recommendation: On the current-account and index pages, keep only the figures that carry the offer itself (fee, bonus, headline conditions) in the main flow and move every supporting number into a secondary block; test the trimmed page against the current one.

recommendations.title: Add more calls to action
recommendations.finding: Calls to action is ING's largest negative gap: 3.0 per page against a peer mean of 13.75, 0.95 standard deviations below. The opening image occupies 0.53 of the page against a peer mean of 0.29, so the few calls to action that exist compete with imagery for attention.
recommendations.recommendation: Repeat one primary call to action at the top, immediately after the offer block and at the end of the current-account and opening-account pages, so that no section of the page ends without a next step.

recommendations.title: Put conditions beside every 'free' claim
recommendations.finding: ING shows 'free' with conditions attached more often than its peers: 0.5 against a peer mean of 0.2, 0.75 standard deviations above. This feature was scored by a model on a sample of human labels, so treat it as a signal to check on the live pages rather than a precise measurement.
recommendations.recommendation: On the current-account and index pages, place the qualifying conditions directly next to each 'free' claim instead of in a footnote or a separate conditions block further down the page.

recommendations.title: Add an explicit mobile-first layout signal
recommendations.finding: Designed mobile-first is absent from ING's pages (0.0) against a peer mean of 0.33, while challenger pages in the same set score 0.67. This is a rubric judgement by the people who scored the pages, so inter-rater agreement matters when reading it.
recommendations.recommendation: Rework the current-account and opening-account pages so that the offer, the price and the primary call to action form a single readable column at mobile width before any desktop-only element (side-by-side text and image, wide tables) is added.

recommendations.title: Shorten the campaign pages
recommendations.finding: Page length is 9,465 px against a peer mean of 6,610.5, 0.72 standard deviations above, and ING already quotes more than twice the peer mean of figures on the same pages. Longer pages here go together with more numbers rather than with more offer.
recommendations.recommendation: Collapse or remove the repeating benefit blocks and duplicated conditions at the bottom of the current-account and index pages, so the offer and its conditions fit into noticeably fewer screens.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table
recommendations.finding: Includes a comparison table is 0.0 for ING against a peer mean of 0.4, one of ING's clearest structural gaps (0.82 standard deviations below). The feature is detected automatically, so this is a clean count rather than a judgement.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a compact pack-comparison table to the current-account page and a package overview to the index page, lining up the monthly fee, the card and the included services across ING's own packs.

recommendations.title: Shrink the opening image
recommendations.finding: Size of the opening image is 0.53 of the page against a peer mean of 0.29, 0.9 standard deviations above, while calls to action sit well below the peer mean at 3.0 against 13.75. The opening image is the largest single element ING commits to before the offer appears.
recommendations.recommendation: Reduce the opening image on the index and current-account pages and use the freed space to bring the offer and one call to action above the fold.

recommendations.title: Give the student messages their own calls to action
recommendations.finding: Targets students or young people is 1.0 for ING against a peer mean of 0.3, 1.53 standard deviations above — a model-assisted score, so weaker evidence than the automatic counts — while the same pages carry the profile's weakest call-to-action density (3.0 against 13.75).
recommendations.recommendation: On the young-customers page, attach a direct call to action and the conditions of any free offer to each student message rather than leaving all of them to one closing block, and mirror the same pattern on the opening-account page.

recommendations.title: Be ready for the early-September current-account window
recommendations.finding: Search interest in ING's current-account terms moved in early September 2026: 'compte à vue ING' shows a sustained trend on 30 August and 6 September 2026 (index 2, score 2.05) and 'ING zichtrekening' an isolated spike on 6 September 2026 (index 7, score 1.63). The same context records an older isolated spike for 'ING zichtrekening' on 22 September 2024 (index 19, score 4.71), and the September 2026 readings are matched to the 'Level up your banking' campaign waves one and eight days earlier, with some rows flagged for seasonal confounding. This is an attention pattern, not proof that any page or campaign caused anything; the link is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Have the current-account page's pack offer, pricing and primary call to action finalised and live before the early-September window, and check that the French-language entry path is as ready as the Dutch one.
recommendations.market_context: A sustained-trend pattern on ING's current-account search terms on 30 August and 6 September 2026, plus a Dutch-language isolated spike on 6 September 2026, inside the search window running 2021-09-12 to 2026-09-13.

recommendations.title: Prepare the savings page in the same window
recommendations.finding: 'compte épargne ING' shows a sustained trend on 6 September 2026 and again on 13 September 2026, matched to the same 'Level up your banking' campaign with delays of 1 and 8 days; the 13 September reading is the one that is not flagged as seasonally confounded. Whether the searches reflect the campaign is unproven, and no search figure says anything about what any page achieved.
recommendations.recommendation: Schedule the savings page refresh into the same delivery slot as the current-account page, completed ahead of the 6 September 2026 window, so the page is not being edited while that attention is open.
recommendations.market_context: Repeated sustained-trend readings on ING's French savings term on 6 and 13 September 2026, the second without a seasonal-confound flag, in a window ending 2026-09-13.

recommendations.title: Set a standing refresh point for the account-pack season
recommendations.finding: KBC, which is also covered by this search context, shows repeated isolated spikes on 'KBC zichtrekening' on 31 August 2025 (index 27, score 2.354), 16 March 2026 (index 21, score 1.743), 17 May 2026 (index 19, score 1.539) and 26 July 2026 (index 25, score 2.15), and on 'Compte Plus KBC' on 10 August 2025 (index 21, score 10.027) — a recurring pattern across seasons, against a single ING account-term spike on 22 September 2024. This is weak, indirect evidence of category seasonality and it covers only the banks marked as covered; it is explicitly a hypothesis, not an outcome.
recommendations.recommendation: Set a standing internal review point ahead of the late-summer period each year at which the current-account and index pages are refreshed, so the pack offer is current before that window rather than during it.
recommendations.market_context: Recurring isolated spikes in KBC's Dutch current-account search term across late summer 2025 and March, May and July 2026, against a single ING account-term spike on 22 September 2024, within a window ending 2026-09-13.
